title: M6.4 EARTHQUAKE Near EASTER ISLAND! What Happened? #shorts
description:
A magnitude 6.4 earthquake struck the South Pacific on October 29, 2026 at 07:49 UTC, according to the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS). The epicenter was in the open ocean about 1,480 km southeast of Hanga Roa, Easter Island (Rapa Nui), not on the island itself.

What USGS reports:
- Magnitude: M6.4 (Mww, reviewed)
- Depth: 10 km, a depth fixed by USGS for a shallow event rather than measured
- PAGER alert: green, a low likelihood of casualties and damage. USGS estimates that no population was exposed to the shaking. PAGER is a model estimate, not a damage report.
- Fault motion: strike-slip (sideways), from the USGS moment tensor

Tsunami: the Pacific Tsunami Warning Center issued no message for this earthquake, and we found no tsunami warning reported for Easter Island or Chile. No damage or injuries have been reported. This may change as more information becomes available.

Why here? The quake struck on the Chile Rise, the boundary where the Nazca and Antarctic plates spread apart. The ridge is broken into segments by faults that slip sideways. USGS recorded a magnitude 6.7 earthquake about 26 km from this epicenter on February 3, 2021.

Official event page: https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/eventpage/us7000ttxz

This video contains altered or synthetic content. The opening image is an AI-generated illustration of Easter Island made with ElevenLabs. It is not a photograph or footage of the earthquake or of any effects on the island.

Credits: earthquake data USGS (public domain). Map data Natural Earth (public domain). Narration ElevenLabs (voice: Daniel). Music: "Deified" by The Grey Room / Density & Time, YouTube Audio Library. Sound effects synthesized for this video.
